title: Blind 75
summary: Original practice versions of the 75 problems on the widely shared Blind 75 interview list. A community study plan, not an official or verified question list.
lesson:
About this list
- Blind 75 is a widely shared list of 75 interview problems that together cover the patterns most coding interviews draw on: arrays and hashing, two pointers, sliding windows, binary search, bit manipulation, dynamic programming, graphs, intervals, linked lists, matrices, trees, tries, and heaps.
- Every problem here is an original practice version written for this plugin. Titles, statements, examples, and tests are our own, so details can differ from versions you find elsewhere.
- The list is a community study plan, not an official or verified set of questions from any company.

What to expect
- The problems are short and well specified, so the challenge is recognizing the pattern quickly and handling edge cases without prompting.
- Many problems share a technique with a neighbor in the list; solving them back to back shows how one idea transfers.
- Interviewers commonly ask for a brute-force idea first, then an improvement, with the time and space complexity of each.

How to prepare
- Work through one category at a time, then revisit the list in mixed order to practice recognizing the pattern without the topic label.
- State the contract questions and the brute-force complexity before opening any hint.
- Aim to pass the full check on the first attempt, and note every missed edge case.
- Revisit problems you passed after a few days and solve them again from a blank starter.
